decisions.decision: Two-bus test subjects for build_message_index tests: M195_Pedal_Press_Percent (bus1 -> MAIN) and Battery_Volt_1_Overall_Param_Std (bus2 -> SENSOR)
decisions.rationale: Both are on config/logger.json's telemetry allowlist; verified via assign_rates(dbc, gate_config) that they resolve to bus1/bus2 respectively, and M195_Pedal_Press_Percent is already the SUBJECT_MESSAGE test_end_to_end.py uses, so reusing it keeps the two test files' fixtures aligned.

decisions.decision: Verified empirically (ad hoc script, not yet a checked-in test) that build_message_index over the real DBC + config/logger.json + config/gate.json produces zero (channel, id_key) collisions across all 128 DBC messages
decisions.rationale: De-risks test_real_dbc_message_index_has_no_collisions before writing it -- confirms the plan's collision-detection design is safe against the real DBC, not just a synthetic case.

decisions.decision: test_duplicate_message_id_key_raises will use synthetic minimal fake message objects (name/frame_id/senders/cycle_time/is_extended_frame attributes only) wrapped in a fake db.messages list, with a sender name absent from gate_config.bus_assignment.by_ecu so _resolve_bus falls back to bus_assignment.default_bus (='bus1' in the real gate.json) -- two fake messages sharing one frame_id then collide under the same MAIN channel
decisions.rationale: The real DBC has zero collisions (see above), so GroundStateError's raise path needs a synthetic forcing case; reusing the real gate_config's default_bus fallback avoids inventing a second config-loading path in the test.

decisions.decision: SseHubCounters guards ONLY clients_connected/clients_peak with an embedded lock (_client_count_lock); frames_dropped_oldest, client_write_failures, and write_failure_log_suppressed_count are left as unguarded simple increments
decisions.rationale: Matches the plan's explicit instruction and FanOutCounters' established convention: only genuinely compound read-modify-write fields (here, the max()-based peak tracking) get a lock; simple per-event increments accept rare lost-update races as diagnostic imprecision, exactly as fanout.py's non-high-water-mark counters do.

decisions.decision: Task 1's SseHub.broadcast() uses a plain put_nowait guarded by queue.Full (bare pass, no counting) -- the tracer's single path per the plan's own text -- and will be replaced by a drop-oldest wrapper in Task 2, not amended in place
decisions.rationale: PLAN.md Task 1 action text explicitly scopes the naive push to Task 1 and assigns the drop-oldest replacement to Task 2's TDD cycle; keeping them as two separate edits preserves clean atomic per-task commits.
